title: Golden Horde: a steppe center
hook: Was the Golden Horde simply a moving army?

knows: Events happen in places and at different times.

objective: Sarai anchors a history often pictured only as cavalry in motion.

claims.text: 1236–40: Western conquests. Batu’s forces conquer the western steppe.
claims.source: https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/golden-horde/ — Golden Horde: Batu, Sarai, 1359 conflict and fifteenth-century fragmentation

claims.text: Mid-1200s: A center. Sarai develops on the lower Volga.
claims.source: https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/golden-horde/ — Golden Horde: Batu, Sarai, 1359 conflict and fifteenth-century fragmentation

claims.text: 1359: Civil conflict. Succession conflict fractures central authority.
claims.source: https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/golden-horde/ — Golden Horde: Batu, Sarai, 1359 conflict and fifteenth-century fragmentation

claims.text: 1400s: Successor states. The Horde fragments into smaller states.
claims.source: https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/golden-horde/ — Golden Horde: Batu, Sarai, 1359 conflict and fifteenth-century fragmentation

claims.text: Sarai anchors a history often pictured only as cavalry in motion. The Golden Horde developed an administrative center on the lower Volga. Later succession conflict and fragmentation changed that political network. A conquest map alone cannot show how authority was organized or lost.
claims.source: https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/golden-horde/ — Golden Horde: Batu, Sarai, 1359 conflict and fifteenth-century fragmentation
